messages:
olivia: kicking off a quick sync on the 'adaptive bench window' idea for onboarding. posted the design doc in google drive. TL;DR: dynamically pick golden sample windows by traffic heatmaps instead of fixed shards.
mike: curious — main win is coverage vs cost? what's the tradeoff on flakiness?
olivia: exactly. static shards miss tail patterns; adaptive windows aim to surface regressions more likely to hit prod. cost is bookkeeping + occasional re-sampling noise.
zhen: how do you pick windows? time-based buckets or input-characteristics?
olivia: pipeline: 1) ingest recent real traffic (7d) 2) cluster by seqlen + embedding-profile + request-route 3) pick top-K windows per cluster weighted by qps. K defaults to 3.
ethan: won't that introduce dataset drift in onboarding? new models could be optimised for recent traffic and overfit.
olia: (typo) olivia: good call — we add a held-out canonical shard that's stable for baseline regression detection. adaptive windows are secondary alerts.
mike: what about determinism for golden comparisons? we need reproducible artifacts for postmortems.
zhen: we can seed samplers with a fixed RNG per-run and snapshot selected examples into the registry. That keeps runs reproducible even if windows shift.
qa-bot: (automated) note: any change that affects golden selection must pass the "repro-playback" smoke in CI. See onboarding-checklist#playback.
lia: question: how do we handle example weighting? heavy-tail inputs should be more sensitive but we don't want to swamp the bench with lots of noisy short requests.
olivia: plan: per-example score = alpha * qps_weight + beta * failure_sensitivity + gamma * diversity_score. alpha,beta,gamma are tunables stored in model-profile. default alpha=0.6 beta=0.3 gamma=0.1.
ethan: can we compute failure_sensitivity from historical KL spikes or regen counts?
zhen: yes — we already have per-input regression history in bench-metrics. use exponential decay window.
mike: ops question: how expensive is full sweep of adaptive windows? any throttles?
olia: (typo) olivia: full sweep is about ~2x current golden cost worst-case. we gate full sweep on onboarding budget and first do a quick mini-sweep (K=1) then escalate.
lia: what about admission criteria? do we change thresholds when using adaptive windows?
olivia: admission remains: canonical shard < threshold A. Adaptive windows can raise warnings or require manual triage if they exceed B. we'll codify levels: info/warn/block.
ethan: how to backfill historical models? we need baseline embeddings to compute diversity-score.
zhen: backfill job can sample 30d historical traffic and compute cluster centroids — incremental job. we can run it weekly.
mike: I want a fallback if traffic ingestion fails (ACLs, S3 issues). Don't want onboarding to stall.
olia: (typo) olivia: fallback = static canonical shards. also pipeline marks adaptive as optional in intake manifest.
qa-bot: (automated) checklist item created: ONB-501 "adaptive bench window: implement seeded repro + canonical fallback" assigned to eng-ml.
olivia: next steps: 1) zhen prototype selector and seeding (PR target: next week) 2) mike/ethan add admission-level hooks in bench-runner 3) lia/qa define sample scoring parameters and alerts.
mike: i'll own bench-runner hooks. will spike the impact on runtime and we can flag gate points.
zhen: starting prototyping. posting WIP notebook link in #eng-ml later today.
ethan: if prototype looks good, let's schedule a 30min design review before we change onboarding RFDs.
lia: ack, I'll prepare alert playbook and triage runbook for adaptive hits.
olivia: thanks all — want minimal surprise for teams. I'll drop a summary in the doc and ping infra for S3 read access.
